metadata.name: Azure Landing Zone Review
metadata.enhancement_notes: All queries enhanced: null-safe (iff/isnotempty), context columns (name, resourceGroup, subscriptionId), checkItem/currentValue/expectedValue fields
metadata.merge_notes: Original 49 enhanced queries + 86 additional queries merged into single file

queries.category: Azure Billing and Microsoft Entra ID Tenants
queries.text: Use one Entra tenant for managing your Azure resources, unless you have a clear regulatory or business requirement for multi-tenants.

queries.category: Azure Billing and Microsoft Entra ID Tenants
queries.text: Use Multi-Tenant Automation approach to managing your Microsoft Entra ID Tenants.

queries.category: Azure Billing and Microsoft Entra ID Tenants
queries.text: Use Azure Lighthouse for Multi-Tenant Management with the same IDs.

queries.category: Azure Billing and Microsoft Entra ID Tenants
queries.text: If you give a partner access to administer your tenant, use Azure Lighthouse.

queries.text: If you have a CSP partner, define and document your support request and escalation process.

queries.category: Azure Billing and Microsoft Entra ID Tenants
queries.text: Setup Cost Reporting and Views with Azure Cost Management.

queries.text: Define and document a process to periodically audit the agreement billing RBAC role assignments to review who has access to your MCA billing account.
Enforce a RBAC model that aligns to your cloud operating model. Scope and Assign across Management Groups and Subscriptions.

queries.subcategory: Microsoft Entra ID and Hybrid Identity
queries.text: Use managed identities instead of service principals for authentication to Azure services. You can check for existing service principals via Entra ID > Sign in Logs > Service principal logins.
queries.graph: resources | where isnotempty(identity) | extend identityType=tostring(identity.type) | project id, name, type, resourceGroup, subscriptionId, checkItem='Managed Identity', currentValue=identityType, expectedValue='SystemAssigned/UserAssigned', compliant=iff(identityType has 'SystemAssigned' or identityType has 'UserAssigned', true, false)

queries.text: Only use the authentication type Work or school account for all account types. Avoid using the Microsoft account (MSA) account type.
Use Microsoft Entra groups to assign permissions. Add on-premises groups to the Entra ID only group if a group management system is already in place.
queries.graph: authorizationresources | where type =~ 'microsoft.authorization/roleassignments' | extend principalType=tostring(properties.principalType) | summarize count() by principalType | project checkItem='RBAC Principal Types', principalType, currentValue=strcat(principalType, ': ', tostring(count_)), expectedValue='Group-based preferred', compliant=iff(principalType =~ 'Group', true, false)

queries.text: Enforce Microsoft Entra ID Conditional Access policies for any user with rights to Azure environments.
Enforce multi-factor authentication for any user with rights to the Azure environments.
Enforce centralized and delegated responsibilities to manage resources deployed inside the landing zone, based on role and security requirements.
Enforce Microsoft Entra ID Privileged Identity Management (PIM) to establish zero standing access and least privilege.

Microsoft recommends that you use roles with the fewest permissions. Global Administrator is a highly privileged role that should be limited to emergency scenarios when you can't use an existing role.
When deploying Active Directory Domain Controllers, use a location with Availability Zones and deploy at least two VMs across these zones. If not available, deploy in an Availability Set.
queries.graph: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.compute/virtualmachines' | where tolower(name) contains 'dc' or tolower(name) contains 'adds' | extend zoneCount=array_length(zones) | extend compliant = iff(zoneCount >= 1, true, false) | project id, name, resourceGroup, subscriptionId, checkItem='DC in AZ', currentValue=iff(zoneCount > 0, tostring(zones), 'No AZ'), expectedValue='Availability Zone', compliant

queries.text: Deploy your Azure landing zone identity resources in multiple regions.  If using domain controllers, associate each region with an Active Directory site so that resources can resolve to their local domain controllers.

Use Azure custom RBAC roles for the following key roles to provide fine-grain access across your ALZ: Azure platform owner, network management, security operations, subscription owner, application owner. Align these roles to teams and responsibilities within your business.
queries.graph: authorizationresources | where type =~ 'microsoft.authorization/roledefinitions' | where properties.type =~ 'CustomRole' | project id, name=tostring(properties.roleName), checkItem='Custom RBAC Roles', currentValue=tostring(properties.roleName), expectedValue='Custom roles for key functions', compliant=true

queries.text: If planning to switch from Active Directory Domain Services to Entra domain services, evaluate the compatibility of all workloads.
When using Microsoft Entra Domain Services, use replica sets. Replica sets will improve the resiliency of your managed domain and allow you to deploy to additional regions.
queries.graph: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.aad/domainservices' | extend replicaCount=array_length(properties.replicaSets) | extend compliant = iff(replicaCount >= 2, true, false) | project id, name, resourceGroup, subscriptionId, checkItem='Entra DS Replicas', currentValue=strcat(tostring(replicaCount), ' set(s)'), expectedValue='2+', compliant

queries.text: Integrate Microsoft Entra ID logs with the platform-central Azure Monitor. Azure Monitor allows for a single source of truth around log and monitoring data in Azure, giving organizations a cloud native options to meet requirements around log collection and retention.

Implement an emergency access or break-glass accounts to prevent tenant-wide account lockout. MFA will be turned on by default for all users in Oct 2024. We recommend updating these accounts to use passkey (FIDO2) or configure certificate-based authentication for MFA.
When deploying Microsoft Entra Connect, use a staging sever for high availability/disaster recovery.
Do not use on-premises synced accounts for Microsoft Entra ID role assignments, unless you have a scenario that specifically requires it.
When using Microsoft Entra ID Application Proxy to give remote users access to applications, manage it as a Platform resource.
Configure Identity network segmentation through the use of a virtual Network and peer back to the hub. Providing authentication inside application landing zone (legacy).
queries.graph: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.network/virtualnetworks/virtualnetworkpeerings' | extend remoteVnet=tostring(properties.remoteVirtualNetwork.id) | extend peerState=tostring(properties.peeringState) | extend compliant = iff(peerState =~ 'Connected', true, false) | project id, name, resourceGroup, subscriptionId, checkItem='VNet Peering State', currentValue=strcat('State: ', peerState, ', Remote: ', tostring(split(remoteVnet,'/')[-1])), expectedValue='Connected', compliant

queries.text: Use Azure RBAC to manage data plane access to resources, if possible. E.g. Data Operations across Key Vault, Storage Account and Database Services.
Use Microsoft Entra ID PIM access reviews to periodically validate resource entitlements.
Restrict and minimize the number of account owners within the enrollment to limit administrator access to subscriptions and associated Azure resources.
queries.graph: authorizationresources | where type =~ 'microsoft.authorization/roleassignments' | extend roleId=tostring(properties.roleDefinitionId) | where roleId endswith '8e3af657-a8ff-443c-a75c-2fe8c4bcb635' | summarize ownerCount=count() | project checkItem='Owner Assignments', currentValue=strcat(tostring(ownerCount), ' Owner role assignments'), expectedValue='Minimize owners', compliant=iff(ownerCount <= 5, true, false)

queries.text: Identify and restrict platform administrators in line with sovereignty requirements (for example, EU‑only, UK‑only, or country‑specific privileged roles).
Use a well defined naming scheme for resources, such as Microsoft Best Practice Naming Standards.
Enforce reasonably flat management group hierarchy with no more than four levels.
queries.graph: resourcecontainers | where type =~ 'microsoft.resources/subscriptions' | extend mgChain=properties.managementGroupAncestorsChain | extend mgDepth=array_length(mgChain) | project id, name, subscriptionId, checkItem='MG Depth', currentValue=strcat(tostring(mgDepth), ' levels'), expectedValue='Max 4 levels', compliant=iff(mgDepth <= 4, true, false)

queries.text: Enforce a sandbox management group to allow users to immediately experiment with Azure.
queries.graph: resourcecontainers | where type == 'microsoft.management/managementgroups' | extend displayName = coalesce(tostring(properties.displayName), name), displayNameLower = tolower(displayName) | extend compliant = iff(displayNameLower has 'sandbox', 1, 0) | project name = displayName, id, compliant

queries.text: Enforce a platform management group under the root management group to support common platform policy and Azure role assignment.
queries.graph: resourcecontainers | where type == 'microsoft.management/managementgroups' | extend displayName = coalesce(tostring(properties.displayName), name), displayNameLower = tolower(displayName) | extend compliant = iff(displayNameLower has 'platform', 1, 0) | project name = displayName, id, compliant

queries.text: Enforce a dedicated connectivity subscription in the Connectivity management group to host an Azure Virtual WAN hub, private non-AD Domain Name System (DNS), ExpressRoute circuit, and other networking resources.
queries.graph: resourcecontainers | where type == 'microsoft.resources/subscriptions' | extend subscriptionId = name, mgmtChainText = tolower(tostring(properties.managementGroupAncestorsChain)) | where mgmtChainText has 'connectivity' | join kind=leftouter (resources | where type in~ ('microsoft.network/virtualwans','microsoft.network/virtualhubs','microsoft.network/expressroutecircuits','microsoft.network/privatednszones','microsoft.network/dnsresolvers') | summarize resourceCount = count() by subscriptionId) on subscriptionId | extend compliant = iff(toint(coalesce(resourceCount, 0)) > 0, 1, 0) | project name, subscriptionId, resourceCount, compliant

queries.text: Enforce no subscriptions are placed under the root management group.
queries.graph: resourcecontainers | where type =~ 'microsoft.resources/subscriptions' | extend mgParent=tostring(properties.managementGroupAncestorsChain[0].name) | extend isUnderRoot = iff(array_length(properties.managementGroupAncestorsChain) <= 1, true, false) | where isUnderRoot == true | project id, name, subscriptionId, checkItem='Sub Under Root MG', currentValue=strcat('Direct parent: ', mgParent), expectedValue='Not under Root MG', compliant=false

queries.text: Enforce that only privileged users can operate management groups in the tenant by enabling Azure RBAC authorization in the management group hierarchy settings.
Enforce management groups under the root-level management group to represent the types of workloads, based on their security, compliance, connectivity, and feature needs.
Enforce a process to make resource owners aware of their roles and responsibilities, access review, budget review, policy compliance and remediate when necessary.
Ensure that all subscription owners and IT core team are aware of subscription quotas and the impact they have on provision resources for a given subscription.
Use Reserved Instances where appropriate to optimize cost and ensure available capacity in target regions.
Establish dashboards and/or visualizations to monitor compute and storage capacity metrics. (i.e. CPU, memory, disk space)
As part of your cloud adoption, implement a detailed cost management plan using the 'Managed cloud costs' process.

If servers will be used for Identity services, like domain controllers, establish a dedicated identity subscription in the identity management group, to host these services. Make sure that resources are set to use the domain controllers available in their region.
Ensure tags are used for billing and cost management.
queries.graph: resources | extend hasTag=isnotempty(tags) | summarize total=count(), tagged=countif(hasTag) | project checkItem='Resource Tagging', currentValue=strcat(tostring(tagged), '/', tostring(total), ' resources tagged (', tostring(round(todouble(tagged)/todouble(total)*100, 1)), '%)'), expectedValue='All resources tagged', compliant=iff(tagged == total, true, false)

queries.text: For Sovereign Landing Zone, have a 'confidential corp' and 'confidential online' management group directly under the 'landing zones' MG.

Select the right Azure region/s for your deployment. Azure is a global-scale cloud platform that provide global coverage through many regions and geographies. Different Azure regions have different characteristics, access and availability models, costs, capacity, and services offered, then it is important to consider all criteria and requirements.

Deploy your Azure landing zone in a multi-region deployment. Depending on customer size, locations, and users presence, operating in multiple regions can be a common choice to deliver services and run applications closer to them. Using a multi-region deployment is also important to provide geo disaster recovery capabilities, to eliminate the dependency from a single region capacity and diminish the risk of a temporary and localized resource capacity constraint.
Ensure required services and features are available within the chosen deployment regions.
For Sovereign Landing Zone, use the management group structure for Public, Confidential Corp, and Confidential Online.
queries.graph: resourcecontainers | where type == 'microsoft.management/managementgroups' | extend displayName = tolower(coalesce(tostring(properties.displayName), name)) | extend compliant = iff(displayName in ('public','confidential corp','confidential online') or displayName has 'confidential corp' or displayName has 'confidential online', 1, 0) | project name = coalesce(tostring(properties.displayName), name), id, compliant

queries.text: Define data classification levels used in your organization.
Use tags to capture sovereign workload metadata such as data classification.
queries.graph: resources | extend dataClassification = coalesce(tostring(tags['DataClassification']), tostring(tags['dataClassification']), tostring(tags['Classification']), tostring(tags['classification'])) | extend compliant = iff(isnotempty(dataClassification), 1, 0) | project name, id, dataClassification, compliant

queries.text: Document a standard for securing the delivery application content from your Workload spokes using Application Gateway and Azure Front Door.  You can use the Application Delivery checklist to for recommendations.
Use a hub-and-spoke network topology for network scenarios that require maximum flexibility.
queries.graph: resources | where type == 'microsoft.network/virtualnetworks/virtualnetworkpeerings' | extend remoteVnetId = tostring(properties.remoteVirtualNetwork.id), peeringName = name | extend compliant = iff(tolower(peeringName) has 'hub' or tolower(remoteVnetId) has 'hub', 1, 0) | project name, id, remoteVnetId, compliant

queries.text: Deploy your Azure landing zone connectivity resources in multiple regions, so that you can quickly support multi-region application landing zones and disaster recovery scenarios.
queries.graph: resources | where type in~ ('microsoft.network/virtualwans','microsoft.network/virtualhubs','microsoft.network/virtualnetworkgateways','microsoft.network/azurefirewalls','microsoft.network/expressroutecircuits') | summarize regionCount = dcount(location), regions = make_set(location) | extend compliant = iff(regionCount > 1, 1, 0) | project regionCount, regions, compliant

queries.text: Deploy shared networking services, including ExpressRoute gateways, VPN gateways, and Azure Firewall or partner NVAs in the central-hub virtual network. If necessary, also deploy DNS services.
queries.graph: resources | where type in~ ('microsoft.network/virtualnetworkgateways','microsoft.network/azurefirewalls','microsoft.network/dnsresolvers','microsoft.network/expressroutecircuits','microsoft.network/privatednszones') | extend compliant = 1 | project name, id, type, location, compliant

queries.text: When deploying partner networking technologies or NVAs, follow the partner vendor's guidance.
If you need transit between ExpressRoute and VPN gateways in hub and spoke scenarios, use Azure Route Server.
queries.graph: resources | where type == 'microsoft.network/routeservers' | extend compliant = 1 | project name, id, location, compliant

queries.text: If using Route Server, use a /27 prefix for the Route Server subnet.
queries.graph: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.network/virtualnetworks' | mv-expand subnets=properties.subnets | where subnets.name =~ 'RouteServerSubnet' | extend prefix=tostring(subnets.properties.addressPrefix) | extend prefixLen=toint(split(prefix, '/')[1]) | extend compliant = iff(prefixLen <= 27, true, false) | project id, name, resourceGroup, subscriptionId, checkItem='RouteServer Subnet', currentValue=prefix, expectedValue='/27 or larger', compliant

queries.text: For network architectures with multiple hub-and-spoke topologies across Azure regions, use global virtual network peerings between the hub VNets to connect the regions to each other.
queries.graph: resources | where type == 'microsoft.network/virtualnetworks/virtualnetworkpeerings' | extend remoteVnetId = tostring(properties.remoteVirtualNetwork.id), localVnetName = tostring(split(id, '/')[8]), remoteVnetName = tostring(split(remoteVnetId, '/')[8]), localVnetId = substring(id, 0, indexof(id, '/virtualNetworkPeerings/')) | join kind=leftouter (resources | where type == 'microsoft.network/virtualnetworks' | project localVnetId = id, localLocation = location) on localVnetId | join kind=leftouter (resources | where type == 'microsoft.network/virtualnetworks' | project remoteVnetId = id, remoteLocation = location) on remoteVnetId | where tolower(localVnetName) has 'hub' and tolower(remoteVnetName) has 'hub' | extend compliant = iff(localLocation != remoteLocation, 1, 0) | project name, id, localLocation, remoteLocation, compliant

queries.text: Use Azure Monitor for Networks to monitor the end-to-end state of the networks on Azure.
queries.graph: resources | summarize networkWatchers = countif(type == 'microsoft.network/networkwatchers'), connectionMonitors = countif(type in~ ('microsoft.network/networkwatchers/connectionmonitors','microsoft.network/connectionmonitors')) | extend compliant = iff(networkWatchers > 0 and connectionMonitors > 0, 1, 0) | project networkWatchers, connectionMonitors, compliant

queries.text: If you have more than 400 spoke networks in a region, deploy an additional hub to bypass VNet peering limits (500) and the maximum number of prefixes that can be advertised via ExpressRoute (1000).
queries.graph: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.network/virtualnetworks' | mv-expand peering=properties.virtualNetworkPeerings | summarize spokeCount=count() by id, name, resourceGroup, subscriptionId, location | project id, name, resourceGroup, subscriptionId, checkItem='Hub Spoke Count', currentValue=strcat(tostring(spokeCount), ' peerings in ', location), expectedValue='Add hub if >400 spokes', compliant=iff(spokeCount <= 400, true, false)

queries.text: Limit the number of routes per route table to 400.
queries.graph: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.network/routetables' | extend routeCount=array_length(properties.routes) | extend compliant = iff(routeCount <= 400, true, false) | project id, name, resourceGroup, subscriptionId, checkItem='Route Count', currentValue=strcat(tostring(routeCount), ' routes'), expectedValue='Max 400', compliant

queries.text: Use the setting 'Allow traffic to remote virtual network' when configuring VNet peerings.
queries.graph: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.network/virtualnetworks' | mv-expand peering=properties.virtualNetworkPeerings | extend allowAccess=tostring(peering.properties.allowVirtualNetworkAccess) | extend peerState=tostring(peering.properties.peeringState) | extend compliant = iff(allowAccess =~ 'true', true, false) | project id, name, resourceGroup, subscriptionId, peeringName=tostring(peering.name), checkItem='Peering Allow Traffic', currentValue=strcat('AllowAccess: ', allowAccess, ', State: ', peerState), expectedValue='true', compliant

queries.text: Use Standard Load Balancer SKU with a zone-redundant deployment, Selecting Standard SKU Load Balancer enhances reliability through availability zones and zone resiliency, ensuring deployments withstand zone and region failures. Unlike Basic, it supports global load balancing and offers an SLA.
queries.graph: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.network/loadbalancers' | extend skuName=tostring(sku.name) | extend skuTier=tostring(sku.tier) | extend compliant = iff(skuName =~ 'Standard', true, false) | project id, name, resourceGroup, subscriptionId, checkItem='Standard LB SKU', currentValue=strcat('SKU: ', skuName, ', Tier: ', iff(isnotempty(skuTier), skuTier, 'N/A')), expectedValue='Standard', compliant

queries.text: Ensure load balancer backend pool(s) contains at least two instances, Deploying Azure Load Balancers with at least two instances in the backend prevents a single point of failure and supports scalability.
queries.graph: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.network/loadbalancers' | mv-expand pool=properties.backendAddressPools | extend backendCount=array_length(pool.properties.loadBalancerBackendAddresses) | extend compliant = iff(backendCount >= 2, true, false) | project id, name, resourceGroup, subscriptionId, poolName=tostring(pool.name), checkItem='LB Backend Size', currentValue=strcat(tostring(backendCount), ' instance(s)'), expectedValue='2+', compliant

queries.text: Is there a requirement to encrypt traffic over the ExpressRoute?
When you're using ExpressRoute Direct, configure MACsec in order to encrypt traffic at the layer-two level between the organization's routers and MSEE. The diagram shows this encryption in flow.
For scenarios where MACsec isn't an option (for example, not using ExpressRoute Direct), use a VPN gateway to establish IPsec tunnels over ExpressRoute private peering.
Ensure no overlapping IP address spaces across Azure regions and on-premises locations are used.
Use IP addresses from the address allocation ranges for private internets (RFC 1918).
queries.graph: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.network/virtualnetworks' | mv-expand addr=properties.addressSpace.addressPrefixes | extend prefix=tostring(addr) | extend isRFC1918 = iff(prefix startswith '10.' or prefix startswith '172.16.' or prefix startswith '192.168.', true, false) | extend compliant = isRFC1918 | project id, name, resourceGroup, subscriptionId, checkItem='RFC1918 Address', currentValue=prefix, expectedValue='RFC1918 range', compliant

queries.text: Ensure that IP address space isn't wasted, don't create unnecessarily large virtual networks (for example /16).
queries.graph: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.network/virtualnetworks' | mv-expand addr=properties.addressSpace.addressPrefixes | extend prefix=tostring(addr) | extend prefixLen=toint(split(prefix, '/')[1]) | project id, name, resourceGroup, subscriptionId, checkItem='VNet Size', currentValue=prefix, expectedValue='Appropriately sized', compliant=iff(prefixLen >= 16, true, false)

queries.text: Do not use overlapping IP address ranges for production and disaster recovery sites.

Use Standard SKU and Zone-Redundant IPs when applicable, Public IP addresses in Azure can be of standard SKU, available as non-zonal, zonal, or zone-redundant. Zone-redundant IPs are accessible across all zones, resisting any single zone failure, thereby providing higher resilience.
queries.graph: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.network/publicipaddresses' | extend skuName=tostring(sku.name) | extend zoneInfo=tostring(zones) | extend compliant = iff(skuName =~ 'Standard', true, false) | project id, name, resourceGroup, subscriptionId, checkItem='Standard Public IP', currentValue=strcat('SKU: ', skuName, ', Zones: ', iff(isnotempty(zoneInfo), zoneInfo, 'None')), expectedValue='Standard, Zone-redundant', compliant

queries.text: For environments where name resolution in Azure is all that's required, use Azure Private DNS for resolution with a delegated zone for name resolution (such as 'azure.contoso.com').
queries.graph: resources | where type == 'microsoft.network/privatednszones' | extend compliant = iff(indexof(name, '.') > 0, 1, 0) | project name, id, compliant

queries.text: For environments where name resolution across Azure and on-premises is required and there is no existing enterprise DNS service like Active Directory, use Azure DNS Private Resolver to route DNS requests to Azure or to on-premises DNS servers.
queries.graph: resources | where type == 'microsoft.network/dnsresolvers' | extend compliant = 1 | project name, id, location, compliant

queries.text: Special workloads that require and deploy their own DNS (such as Red Hat OpenShift) should use their preferred DNS solution.
Enable auto-registration for Azure DNS to automatically manage the lifecycle of the DNS records for the virtual machines deployed within a virtual network.
queries.graph: resources | where type == 'microsoft.network/privatednszones/virtualnetworklinks' | extend registrationEnabled = properties.registrationEnabled | extend compliant = iff(registrationEnabled == true, 1, 0) | project name, id, compliant

queries.text: Implement a plan for managing DNS resolution between multiple Azure regions and when services fail over to another region

Disable Windows systems from attempting to use port 65330 in Azure, Windows systems in Azure may attempt to use port 65330 for DNS resolution, which can cause timeouts and connectivity issues. Disabling this behavior can help prevent these issues.
Use Azure Bastion to securely connect to your network.
queries.graph: resources | where type == 'microsoft.network/bastionhosts' | extend compliant = 1 | project name, id, location, compliant

queries.text: Use Azure Bastion in a subnet /26 or larger.
queries.graph: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.network/virtualnetworks' | mv-expand subnets=properties.subnets | where subnets.name =~ 'AzureBastionSubnet' | extend prefix=tostring(subnets.properties.addressPrefix) | extend prefixLen=toint(split(prefix, '/')[1]) | extend compliant = iff(prefixLen <= 26, true, false) | project id, name, resourceGroup, subscriptionId, checkItem='Bastion Subnet', currentValue=prefix, expectedValue='/26 or larger', compliant

queries.text: Use Azure Front Door and WAF policies to provide global protection across Azure regions for inbound HTTP/S connections to a landing zone.
queries.graph: resources | summarize frontDoors = countif(type == 'microsoft.cdn/profiles' and tostring(sku.name) has 'FrontDoor'), wafPolicies = countif(type in~ ('microsoft.cdn/cdnwebapplicationfirewallpolicies','microsoft.network/frontdoorwebapplicationfirewallpolicies')) | extend compliant = iff(frontDoors > 0 and wafPolicies > 0, 1, 0) | project frontDoors, wafPolicies, compliant

queries.text: When using Azure Front Door and Azure Application Gateway to help protect HTTP/S apps, use WAF policies in Azure Front Door. Lock down Azure Application Gateway to receive traffic only from Azure Front Door.

When WAFs and other reverse proxies are required for inbound HTTP/S connections, deploy them within a landing-zone virtual network and together with the apps that they're protecting and exposing to the internet.
Use Azure DDoS Network or IP Protection plans to help protect Public IP Addresses endpoints within the virtual networks including application landing zones.
queries.graph: resources | where type == 'microsoft.network/virtualnetworks' | extend ddosPlanId = tostring(properties.ddosProtectionPlan.id), ddosEnabled = properties.enableDdosProtection | extend compliant = iff(ddosEnabled == true or isnotempty(ddosPlanId), 1, 0) | project name, id, compliant

queries.text: Plan for how to manage your network outbound traffic configuration and strategy before the upcoming breaking change. On September 30, 2025, default outbound access for new deployments will be retired and only explicit access configurations will be allowed.
Add diagnostic settings to save DDoS related logs for all the protected public IP addresses (DDoS IP or Network Protection).
queries.graph: resources | where type == 'microsoft.insights/diagnosticsettings' | extend lowerId = tolower(id) | where lowerId has '/microsoft.network/publicipaddresses/' or lowerId has '/microsoft.network/ddosprotectionplans/' | extend compliant = 1 | project name, id, compliant

queries.text: Ensure there is a policy assignment to deny Public IP addresses directly tied to Virtual Machines.  Use exclusions if public IPs are needed on specific VMs.
queries.graph: policyresources | where type == 'microsoft.authorization/policyassignments' | extend displayName = tolower(tostring(properties.displayName)), definitionId = tolower(tostring(properties.policyDefinitionId)) | extend compliant = iff(displayName has 'public ip' or definitionId has 'publicip', 1, 0) | project name, id, compliant

queries.text: Use ExpressRoute as the primary connection to Azure.  Use VPNs as a source of backup connectivity.
queries.graph: resources | summarize expressRouteCircuits = countif(type == 'microsoft.network/expressroutecircuits'), vpnGateways = countif(type == 'microsoft.network/virtualnetworkgateways' and tolower(tostring(properties.gatewayType)) == 'vpn') | extend compliant = iff(expressRouteCircuits > 0 and vpnGateways > 0, 1, 0) | project expressRouteCircuits, vpnGateways, compliant

queries.text: When you use multiple ExpressRoute circuits or multiple on-prem locations, use BGP attributes to optimize routing.
Select the right SKU for the ExpressRoute/VPN gateways based on bandwidth and performance requirements.
queries.graph: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.network/virtualnetworkgateways' | where properties.gatewayType =~ 'vpn' or properties.gatewayType =~ 'ExpressRoute' | extend skuName=tostring(properties.sku.name) | extend skuTier=tostring(properties.sku.tier) | extend gwType=tostring(properties.gatewayType) | extend compliant = iff(skuTier !in~ ('Basic','Standard'), true, false) | project id, name, resourceGroup, subscriptionId, checkItem='Gateway SKU', currentValue=strcat(gwType, ': ', skuName), expectedValue='Not Basic/Standard', compliant

queries.text: Ensure that you're using unlimited-data ExpressRoute circuits only if you reach the bandwidth that justifies their cost.
queries.graph: resources | where type =~ 'microsoft.network/expressroutecircuits' | extend skuFamily=tostring(sku.family) | extend bw=tostring(properties.bandwidthInMbps) | extend compliant = iff(skuFamily =~ 'MeteredData', true, false) | project id, name, resourceGroup, subscriptionId, checkItem='ER Data Plan', currentValue=strcat(skuFamily, ', ', bw, ' Mbps'), expectedValue='MeteredData (unless unlimited needed)', compliant

queries.text: Leverage the Local SKU of ExpressRoute to reduce the cost of your circuits, if your circuit peering location supports your Azure regions for the Local SKU.
